title: FUTURESCOMMODITIES — Commodity Futures Paper-Trading Competition
description: Live engine, one strategy roster, twenty explicit instruments and one venue family, with no simulation anywhere. engine/strategies/index.mjs registers exactly 20 strategies and usernames: 9 Kalshi event contracts, 2 Kalshi perpetuals, 5 exchange commodity futures (MOEX FORTS), 1 FX, 1 equity index, 1 interest-rate and 1 cross-venue instrument, each with its declared data source, granularity, time horizon, risk model and sizing rule. config/competition.json fixes the season window 2026-09-22 to 2027-09-22, a $100,000 starting bankroll, 130 ms between engine ticks, a 12-hour history refresh, a 100-series candle cap, taker fills at 25% of visible depth, a 6-hour maker TTL and 0.001 perp participation, with MOEX gates at 10-minute volume, 20-minute open interest, 2% price and 5% open interest. data/reports/summary.json (2026-09-23T00:52:33Z) reports the first live run: 5 ticks, the last with 1,900 instruments, 107 quotes, 26 trades, 3 intents, 181 requests and 0 settlements, with all 20 leaderboard rows equity_complete true at $100,000.00 — an opening equity of 99,839.83, -0.16% — 13 of them carrying open positions and 0 closed trades, 0 fees and 0 slippage. data/verification/report.json checks 132 trades against the official APIs: 98 fully verified, 34 anomalies (28 instrument-universe, 6 cross-venue basis), across 107 instruments (45 kalshi, 12 kalshi_margin, 50 moex_forts), with fill tiers 94 quote-based, 38 ladder and 0 modelled maker. data/reports/backtests.json records 6 backtests and 817 simulated trades, of which moex-metals-trend-10d carries 674 at -9.4448% and moex-metal-breakout-20-10 carries 143 at -4.5481% while the four Kalshi runs each ran 0 trades; 4 strategies are marked unavailable_for_backtesting. MOEX fees are quoted at ISS USD/RUB 84.72 and the repo discloses no depth, slippage or participation model.

flags: Catalog and competition state disagree because the repository moved while it was being read. Commit a64a347 ('Expand to 17 strategies, re-enable cross-venue basis on verified contract data, add research backtests and live-desk/research site sections', 2026-09-22T23:04:47Z) added five strategies and re-enabled @basis-hunter, but the tick it sits on top of was generated at 23:03:54Z and still reports coverage.strategies == 12 with a 12-row leaderboard. Both numbers are published here with the file each came from instead of being reconciled. IRR-75.

All 10 verification anomalies are the same check, instrument_present_in_published_universe — instruments that settled and dropped out of the universe file. They are reported on the site and never silently corrected.

Of the 6 documented backtest rules only two recorded any trades at all (Metals Settlement Trend 674 and Channel Breakout 20/10 on MOEX metals 143); the other four recorded 0. The 817 total is the sum of total_trades_recorded across the six, and the file's own caveat states that a backtest 'is never a track record and never a season trade'. Its fills are at published daily prices with no depth, no slippage, no participation cap and no queue position.

Where an exchange blocks scripted access — CME Group, ICE, LME, Eurex, JPX, SGX, B3 — contract specifications are cited from official pages but no price is simulated, and the strategy is labelled unavailable for backtesting rather than filled from a proxy.

This is a returns-only simulator by design: strategies are deliberately not risk-managed because the competition is scored on returns alone, and the only hard constraints are real liquidity from the published order books and a one-position-per-instrument rule.
